newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian GDP in Q3 "basically stagnant" - Istat.
newsitem.headline: Italian GDP in Q3 "basically stagnant" - Istat.

text.p: Italian gross domestic product (GDP) in the third quarter is expected to be basically stagnant but not recessionary, Italian national statistics office Istat said on Friday.
"The situation emerging in the third quarter confirms this period of largely stagnant production," said Enrico Giovannini, head of Istat's GDP statistics office.
"From indicators available, consumer demand shows signs of being in a depressed stage. In the third quarter, GDP is basically stationary," he said.
"We are not falling, we are in a phase of stagnation not recession," Giovannini said.

He said GDP grew one percent in the first six months of the year. For the economy to meet the government's latest target and grow by 0.8 percent in the whole year, GDP in the last six months of 1996 must increase by 0.6 percent, Giovannini said.
Earlier Istat said Italy's GDP rose by a real 0.7 percent, year-on-year, in the second quarter of 1996, but fell 0.4 percent quarter-on-quarter.
Provisional third quarter GDP data will be released by Istat on November 29.
